Our Vision 2025-2030
We are committed to preparing our students for an ever-changing world, equipping them with the skills, confidence, and resilience to thrive and lead.
Our 2025-2030 vision is a bold strategy built on four key pillars:
Our Vision 2025-2030
Focus on Educational Excellence
We foster a holistic education, combining academic excellence, outstanding support of mental health and wellbeing, and first class co-curricular enrichment within a seamless and joyful journey from Nursery to Sixth Form, where each girl is empowered to exceed her own expectations. As an innovative girls’ school, we continuously evolve our teaching and learning environments to develop emotional intelligence (EQ), intellectual growth (IQ), and digital fluency (DQ), preparing pupils for an interconnected and rapidly changing world. This encompasses the nurturing of the St Helen’s Character Attributes (resilience, integrity, courage, kindness) and Learner Habits (pursuit of knowledge, problem-solving, creativity and metacognition) which underpin all that we do.
Creating Opportunities for All
Every girl is treated as a scholar, with our Academic Enrichment and Scholarship programmes fostering excellence across academic, creative, and sporting fields while providing opportunities to have fun and discover lifelong passions. Committed to widening access, we continue to develop our Bursary Programme and Diversity, Equity, Inclusion and Belonging (DEIB) strategy, ensuring an exceptional education is accessible to all, regardless of financial means or background.
Building Professional Capital
Our motto for all our staff, One School: One Staff: One Purpose, reflects our commitment to excellence, with Governors, Leaders, and Staff serving as role models through expertise and engagement across all departments. By prioritising professional development and innovation while mastering the fundamentals, we ensure every interaction is purposeful and contributes to the pursuit of excellence.
Raising External Profile
This pillar celebrates the achievements of our students and staff while fostering meaningful engagement with stakeholders, the local community, and global academic and business networks. We also cultivate strong connections with our alumnae, who generously share their time and expertise, with a long-term vision to develop a clear and sustainable strategy for maintaining these vital links.
As we embark on this exciting new phase, we invite our students, parents, staff, and alumnae to join us in shaping the future of St Helen’s School. Discover more by exploring our Vision 2025-2030 booklet below.

Welcome
Welcome to St Helen’s
Here you will find a school that believes in your daughter and her individual potential, creativity, and ability, and it is this approach that is embedded in everything we do.
Our passionate, dedicated and deeply knowledgeable teaching staff are highly ambitious for all our students, and they are committed to supporting, encouraging and challenging every girl to be the very best version of themselves.
Exceptional exam results are the foundations of our school, but we know that what happens outside the classroom is also vitally important. Our co-curricular programme offers over 200 clubs and societies, opening a world of opportunity through which, your daughter will be able to discover her talents and passions, but also create and nurture friendships that will last a lifetime.
Our students are supported by our dedicated pastoral programme which ensures that each individual is seen and heard, therefore, allowing every student to leave us with the resilience, critical thinking and fortitude that is required to excel in the 21st Century.
While our website will give you an introduction to what St Helen’s is about, it is impossible to truly grasp all that is St Helen’s here alone. I encourage you and your family to visit and to experience first-hand what makes this school such an exciting and inspiring place.

Welcome
Start your journey here
We are delighted that you are considering St Helen’s School for your daughter. Choosing the right school is an important milestone, and we understand just how meaningful this decision is for your family.
St Helen’s is a vibrant, forward-thinking community where girls are empowered to become the very best versions of themselves. Rooted in a culture of courage, integrity, kindness and resilience, our school offers an inspiring environment in which every girl is known, valued, and supported to thrive academically and personally.
We are an academically selective school, and we welcome girls into Nursery (3+) and Reception (4+), Year 7 (11+) and Sixth Form (16+). Entry into other year groups is possible subject to the availability of a place and families interested in joining outside the usual entry points should contact the admissions team who will be pleased to advise on availability and next steps. We are delighted to offer bursaries and a variety of scholarship awards for entry at 11+ and 16+, allowing talented students to have the opportunity to benefit from all the school has to offer.
Our admissions process is designed to select pupils who will thrive and flourish in the learning environment that is offered at St Helen’s and who will contribute fully to our school community. We aim to understand each girl as an individual, enabling us to take a holistic approach to admissions decisions. Our Admissions Team is here to guide and support you and your daughter through every step of the process. Whether you are just beginning to explore your options or are ready to take the next step, we are committed to helping you discover what makes St Helen’s such a special place to learn and grow.
You will meet us at Open Events and on school tours, where we look forward to welcoming you in person. We are always happy to answer your questions and provide information you may need as you navigate the Admissions process.
Please feel free to contact us on 01923 843230 or email us on admissions@sthelens.london at any stage of your application.
We kindly encourage you to take note of our registration deadlines to ensure your daughter’s application can be fully considered.
Registration deadline dates for entry in 2027
Prep School – Friday 6 November 2026
Senior School – Friday 6 November 2026
Sixth Form – Thursday 15 October 2026
Sixth Form – Thursday 4 February 2027
We’re here to help guide you through our Admissions process
Visit
To get a true sense of St Helen’s School, start by visiting us at one of our Open Events.
Register
Registration is the first step of the Admissions process to secure your daughter a place. Registration is completed online and includes a registration fee, which needs to be submitted at the point of registration.
Assessment
To ensure St Helen’s is the best fit for your child, assessments and where relevant, interviews with your daughter, are held. A reference or school report from your daughter’s current school is also requested.
Offer
Following the interviews, students selected for a place will be sent an offer by email.
Our prospectus offers a clear insight into the exceptional academic, co-curricular, and pastoral opportunities that shape our students into confident, capable, and compassionate young women. Discover how we nurture ambition, celebrate individuality, and inspire success at every stage of their educational journey.
If you’re looking for quick answers to common queries, our Frequently Asked Questions section is a great place to start. You’ll find helpful guidance on everything from entry points to assessment and beyond.
Our Admissions Team would be delighted to discuss all aspects of the process with you.
Please contact us on 01923 843230 or email admissions@sthelens.london.

Outreach & Partnerships
We are rooted in our community and are proud to share our facilities, expertise, knowledge and experience with those around us. Our Outreach and Partnership programme also helps St Helen’s pupils gain valuable skills and experience which are applicable to a range of higher education and career pathways, and which will help prepare them for life beyond school in all sorts of ways.
Our Community
Outreach & Partnerships
Our Outreach and Partnership Programme
Building Stronger Futures Together
At St Helen’s, outreach is more than a programme, it’s a promise. A promise to nurture meaningful connections, widen access to opportunity, and develop future leaders who lead with empathy, purpose, and integrity. Our long-standing commitment to working in partnership with local schools is an integral part of who we are as a community, and our pupils play an active, powerful role in making that happen.
We are proud to collaborate with a growing network of local primary and secondary schools across Northwood and beyond, including:
Together, we deliver inspiring learning experiences that extend beyond the classroom and support every child to thrive.
Greenfields Primary School
Coteford Junior School
Hillside Primary School
Eastbury Farm Primary School
Frithwood Primary School
A Transformational Experience For All
Our Outreach and Partnership programme enriches the educational journeys of children in our local schools, and gives our students real-world experience in mentoring, leadership, and communication. Whether they are leading a drama club, supporting early phonics development, running a sports session or guiding a science experiment, our pupils step up with commitment, creativity and care.
“I really looked forward to helping them each week. Even though we only saw them for a short time, I felt like we made a difference.” — St Helen’s Sixth Form Student
For many of our Sixth Formers, their outreach placements are a defining part of their school journey. They learn how to communicate clearly, plan engaging sessions, build rapport, and reflect on the impact they’re making. It’s also an opportunity to share their passion for learning while gaining essential skills for university, work, and life.
What We Offer
Our programme spans a rich variety of academic and co-curricular opportunities, tailored to the needs of each partner school:
Curriculum Enrichment
Literacy and Phonics Support
Our Sixth Formers receive specialist training to deliver high-quality one-to-one reading support and phonics teaching, helping younger pupils build confidence and early language skills.
Modern Foreign Languages
Early language acquisition is brought to life through Spanish and French workshops, led with enthusiasm and cultural curiosity.
Hands-on sessions in our labs and classrooms spark curiosity in Science, Technology, Engineering and Maths, topics include CSI St Helen’s, Animal Behaviour, Rocket Design, and more.
Creative Arts & Drama
Workshops and clubs that develop imagination, communication and public speaking skills, giving pupils the space to express themselves and build confidence.
From percussion to piano, our pupils run music clubs that build rhythm, coordination and confidence in an inspiring setting.
Activity Days
We host exciting days of immersive learning for pupils from local state schools, offering workshops in everything from Sports Science and Microscopy to printing, origami, orienteering and climbing. Pupils get to experience high-quality facilities and expertise they may not otherwise have access to.
Why It Matters
Partnerships like ours are grounded in mutual respect, shared values, and a commitment to opportunity for all. The impact is wide-reaching and deeply felt:
“Thanks to St Helen’s and their families, our children have increased life chances, better standards of living and experiences… Our partnership is special and better than others we work with locally.” — Mrs Kate Day, Headteacher, Greenfields Primary School
“What really makes this partnership stand out is the personal connection. The atmosphere created when pupils blend in with ours is warm, positive and inclusive.” — Rachael Eckley, Deputy Head, Coteford School
“The quality of learning has improved markedly… The diverse range of clubs and outreach days offered directly at our school give children access to enriching experiences.” — Mrs Kate Gibson, Co-Headteacher, Hillside Infants School
A Foundation for the Future
As our Outreach and Partnership programme continues to grow, we remain focused on:
We are always open to new collaborations. If you are a local school looking to partner with us or want to know more about how we could work together, we’d love to hear from you.
Deepening ties with existing partner schools

pageCache.text:
FIREWORKS NIGHT

At our recent Year 10 Academic and Pastoral Evening, parents heard from Chantal Duarte, Performance Psychologist at InnerDrive, who delivered a talk that explored how parents can support their daughters to become more effective and independent learners during their GCSE years.
Drawing on the science of learning and performance psychology, Chantal shared practical strategies that parents can encourage at home.
From resisting the temptation to multitask, to using retrieval practice rather than simply re-reading notes, the session explored the small habits that can make learning more effective. Parents also heard about the benefits of spacing revision over time, managing procrastination and helping their daughters organise demanding tasks around periods of better concentration.
Chantal also highlighted the vital role of sleep and healthy routines in concentration, decision-making and managing pressure, alongside the importance of helping young people keep setbacks in perspective and respond constructively when things do not go to plan.
The message was clear: academic success is not about pressure or last-minute cramming. It is built through effective habits, consistently practised over time.
We hope our Year 10 parents left feeling re-energised, with a practical toolkit to help their daughters take increasing ownership of their learning and flourish throughout their GCSE studies.
Thank you to Chantal and InnerDrive for an engaging and insightful session.

We are proud to have been recognised with the Young Carers in Schools Award which is a national recognition scheme that awards good practice in identifying and supporting young carers in school.
A young carer is someone aged under 18 who looks after, or helps look after, someone in their family who may have: a long-term health condition, a mental health illness, a disability, Special Educational Needs or someone who misuses drugs or alcohol. It is important to remember that there is no specific look to a young carer – they could be anyone.
We are proud to offer extra support to our young carers because the responsibilities that come with being a young carer can result in these pupils missing school, not being able to get homework done and an added emotional burden. At St Helen’s we have a special Young Carers Team led by Miss Mendis and we are able to offer homework support, emotional support and referrals to other agencies.
Miss Mendis explains what the Young Carers Award means to us to St Helen’s:
“Working towards the Young Carers in Schools Award has been an invaluable journey for our school. The award framework has helped us to identify, recognise and better support our young carers, ensuring that they feel seen, understood and valued within our school community. This has helped to create a culture where young carers are recognised and supported by both staff and their peers.
The award has also encouraged us to share information with parents and carers, many of whom may not previously have recognised that their child had a caring role. As a result, we have been able to identify more young carers and ensure they receive the support they need both in school and through external services.
Thanks to the Young Carers in Schools Award, awareness of young carers is now embedded throughout our school community. We have been able to develop tailored, person-centred support for our young carers, helping them to overcome barriers to learning, improve their wellbeing and fully engage in school life. Most importantly, our young carers know that they are not alone and that there is a network of understanding and support available to them.”

The UK Space Design Competition (UKSDC) is a national STEM challenge for UK pupils in Years 10–13, where teams design a futuristic crewed space settlement and present it to industry judges, with finalists competing at Imperial College London and top performers advancing to the International Space Settlement Design Competition at NASA’s Kennedy Space Centre. This week nine St Helen’s girls from Years 10 and 11 attended the UKSDC.
Written by Akshara, Year 10
On Saturday this week, we had the opportunity to travel to Royal Holloway, University of London, to take part in the UK Space Design Competition (UKSDC). It was a really exciting and fast-paced day, and a great opportunity to meet and work with pupils from other schools.
At the start of the competition, we formed an aerospace company, called Archer Valentine, with pupils from Merchant Taylors’ School and Queensmead School. We were split into different departments and given an RFP (Request for Proposal), which required us to design a future space settlement on Mars, while meeting a specific set of requirements. We had to research our ideas, make decisions and work together to create one final proposal, all within 7 hours!
I worked in Human Engineering and was elected Head of Department, which gave me the opportunity to lead a team and delegate tasks. In our team, we focused on factors such as accommodation, food, health and the overall quality of life of people living in the settlement on Mars. We also had to collaborate and communicate effectively with the other departments, as all of our ideas needed to work together.
At the end of the day, we brought everything together into a final presentation and pitched our proposal to a panel of judges and over 150 others, which was stressful at first, but super fun!
Overall, UKSDC was a great experience that helped us develop our teamwork, leadership, problem-solving and presentation skills. It also allowed us to experience what engineering and the future of space exploration would actually be like. We would definitely recommend the experience to other pupils next year! Thank you so much to Miss Wise for organising the day.

Bridget has predominantly worked in all-girls’ education since qualifying as a teacher in July 2000. Her most recent roles include Head of Merchant Taylors’ Girls’ School, Crosby, and Deputy Head at Woldingham School, Surrey. Prior to these positions, she was a member of the Senior Leadership Team at Queen’s Gate School, London, where she served in various capacities over 11 years.
With over 20 years of experience spanning the pastoral, academic, and co-curricular aspects of school life, Bridget has developed a deep understanding of the holistic nature of education. As a former athlete, she has a particular interest in sports and the transformative power of a successful extracurricular and co-curricular programme, believing that these experiences are essential in shaping individuals and preparing them for the ever-changing world. She advocates for the enrichment of academic studies with outside interests, emphasising that this balance is key to building resilience and developing 21st-century skills.
Bridget is deeply invested in educational research and has pursued continuous learning throughout her career, recently completing an MBA in Educational Leadership from UCL. She is also a Fellow of the Chartered College of Teaching. Her academic research covers a broad range of topics, including school culture, the development of a 21st-century curriculum, the effective use of data, and the creation of consistent habits to build resilience and success in girls.
Since 2015, Bridget has served as an ISI Team Inspector and is currently a serving Reporting Inspector. She is also a Governor of a school in Kent.
Bridget remains active in sports, training early in the morning, and has recently completed an English Channel swim and an Isles of Scilly swim—always keeping an eye on the next challenge.
An experienced Senior Leader and teacher of Mathematics. She has oversight of safeguarding, pastoral provision and pupil welfare across the School, working closely with the Heads of Section in Senior School and the Head of the Prep School.
Before taking up her role at St Helen’s, Neelam was Vice-Principal (Pastoral) at King Edward VI High School for Girls in Birmingham and Assistant Head at Latymer Upper School in Hammersmith. She studied Mathematics, obtaining a First-Class degree and a Master’s from the University of Warwick.
Outside of school, Neelam has been involved in delivering training for NQTs across Birmingham and enjoys playing badminton, cooking and singing.
Jess joined St Helen’s as Assistant Head - Teaching and Learning in 2024. She holds a BA in Geography from the University of Manchester and was most recently the Head of Geography at North London Collegiate School.
She has gained extensive experience over the years from a wide range of diverse educational settings, including international, private, and state sectors. During this time Jess has successfully improved the standards in the various classrooms she oversaw and successfully enhanced the student outcomes and experiences.
As the Assistant Head - Teaching and Learning, Jess is responsible for overseeing and enhancing the quality of teaching, learning, and educational outcomes of St Helen’s.
In her spare time Jess enjoys activities such as hiking and participating in triathlons and serves as a governor at a local state school.
James Bown is the Deputy Head: Academic. Prior to joining St Helen's, James was the Director of Teaching and Learning at Haberdashers' Boys' School, responsible for the quality of education through the school, as well as the development of people across the four Haberdasher Elstree Schools.
James is a leader who strives to deliver excellent and inclusive teaching and learning across all levels and subjects.
His interests, other than his passion for teaching Geography, are in scholarship, curriculum development, empowering middle leaders, and innovation. Outside of the classroom, James enjoys spending time with his family and keeping active outdoors.
Alice has been working at St Helen’s since 2015. Initially appointed as a teacher of MFL (Spanish & French), over the years Alice has held various positions of responsibility including Oxbridge Coordinator, Deputy Director of Futures, Director of Communications and, from September 2024, Assistant Head Engagement and Communications. In this senior role, Alice is responsible for ensuring the smooth transition of pupils across the Prep School, Senior School and Sixth Form. Alongside our Admissions team, she manages the 11+ process and the induction programme for new pupils.
A large part of Alice’s role as Assistant Head Engagement and Communications is to communicate with parents and develop the integral partnership between school and home, ensuring that families feel supported, listened to, informed and involved in their daughter’s educational journey.
Prior to teaching at St Helen’s, Alice taught Spanish and French at two large comprehensive schools in South Devon. Before entering the teaching profession, she studied Modern and Medieval Languages (Spanish & Russian) at the University of Cambridge, and took a year out to pursue floristry and floral design. Outside of school she is kept busy with her two small children and enjoys reading, good coffee and going to the theatre.
Sudeep is a graduate from the University of Surrey, with a BA QTS specialising in Theology and Religious Studies. She joined St Helen’s in 2009 as Maths Coordinator after having worked in a Church of England school in Maida Vale and a well-established local state school.
Being an advocate of well-being, she has a real passion in ensuring the pastoral needs of pupils are met and truly believes pupils flourish when they are happy and in a nurturing environment. Through her own journey of mindfulness, Sudeep has developed the use of mindfulness techniques within the Prep School.
Currently, Sudeep is part of both the Senior Leadership and Prep Leadership Teams and is leading the whole school on developing Character Education and Pupil Coaching within the Prep School.
Outside of school, she enjoys yoga, travelling abroad and spending time with friends and family organising memorable events so they can spend quality time together.
Ros Bryson completed her BA (QTS) at Canterbury Christ Church University. She joined St Helen’s in 2023 as a Year 2 teacher bringing with her over twenty years of experience in the Primary sector in schools across Hertfordshire. She has led Phase teams within all three key stages and been acting deputy. She has led a range of curriculum areas including English and Science where she completed the Primary Science Quality Mark, which not only led to a good improvement in the attainment of the children across the school, but the engagement and enthusiasm of both pupils and staff which grew as the pupils became keen to develop as Scientists.
Since joining the school, she has been one of the representatives on the DEIB committee and led the committee for the whole school ‘Cultural Diversity Day’. As the Director of EYFS to Year 4, Ros brings a wealth of experience to the role to ensure that together we create an exciting, challenging and supportive environment for the pupils to build their independence as learners and trailblazers for the future.
Outside of school, Ros enjoys travelling with her family, reading and singing. She is a keen walker and can often be found supporting her local rugby team.
Carole has worked in education since 2010, gaining experience across both state and independent schools. She has particular expertise in safeguarding and pastoral care, having held safeguarding responsibilities within schools as well as with British Gymnastics.
Outside of school, Carole enjoys spending time with her husband and children. She has been a Girlguiding UK leader for over 20 years and is also a British Gymnastics trampoline judge.
I am extremely passionate about education for girls, creating a nurturing environment to supporting their holistic development and prepare them for the dynamic 21st century. With over two decades of experience in education, I’ve been proud to contribute to the growth and development of pupils at St Helen’s since September 2000. I’m passionate about the evolving role of technology in education and how digital tools can enhance learning experiences and outcomes. I closely follow educational trends and am always looking for innovative ways to support and inspire pupils, ensuring that every learner achieves their full potential.
Beyond the classroom, I’m a lifelong sports enthusiast. I’ve played hockey at a high level and continue to enjoy club hockey. I also love being outdoors and travelling with my family, exploring new places locally and abroad.

Leadership Development
We believe passionately in developing leaders of tomorrow.
Alongside their academic options for GCSE, pupils in Year 9 opt to commit to one of our major co-curriculum programmes. In many cases, they will participate in their chosen programme for up to four years, taking on significant amounts of personal responsibility and the service of others as they build their skills and experiences.
These enable them to develop invaluable skills of leadership, responsibility, teamwork and resilience. In many cases, students will participate in their chosen programme for up to four years, taking on significant amounts of personal responsibility and the service of others as they build their skills and experiences.
The Combined Cadet Force (CCF) is held after school on Friday afternoons at Merchant Taylors’ School. Pupils apply to join either the Royal Navy, Army, or RAF Section of CCF. Cadets develop self-confidence and self-discipline through enjoyable military themed and adventurous activities alongside students from Merchant Taylors’ School which enable them to take responsibility and develop resourcefulness, endurance, perseverance and leadership. In the Sixth Form, many cadets are selected to take on positions of responsibility within the CCF, leading the junior cadets and delivering most of the training activities. Highlights of the CCF year include field days and visits to military establishments, Inspection Day with visiting military VIPs, annual summer camps and a variety of courses and experiences, from static-line parachuting to white-water rafting.
St Helen’s has offered the Duke of Edinburgh’s Award Scheme for many years, and we are very proud to have obtained the status of a Directly Licensed Centre, enabling us to deliver the Duke of Edinburgh’s Award independently on our own premises and using our own staff. Pupils must complete four elements to gain an Award: an Expedition, a Service element, Physical Recreation and a Skill element, providing many opportunities to get involved in a range of activities and to develop new interests. Approximately half of the girls in Years 10 and 11 participate in the Award Scheme, with an impressive number completing their Bronze and Silver Awards before going on to pursue the Gold Award in the Sixth Form. The first cohort of St Helen’s pupils to complete their Gold Awards visited St James’ Palace on the 23rd June 2014 and received their awards from HRH Prince Edward, Earl of Wessex.
